# modifiedHuberGradient

> Compute the [modified Huber loss gradient][modified-huber-loss-gradient] with respect to a model parameter for a single-precision floating-point number.

<section class="intro">

The [modified Huber loss gradient][modified-huber-loss-gradient] is defined as

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:modified_huber_loss_gradient" align="center" raw="
\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial w_i} = \begin{cases} -4yx_i & \text{if } yp < -1 \\ -2y(1 - yp)x_i & \text{if } -1 \le yp \le 1 \\ 0 & \text{if } yp > 1 \end{cases}" alt="Equation for the modified Huber loss gradient."> -->

```math
\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial w_i} =
\begin{cases}
-4yx_i & \text{if } yp < -1 \\
-2y(1 - yp)x_i & \text{if } -1 \le yp \le 1 \\
0 & \text{if } yp > 1
\end{cases}
```

<!-- </equation> -->

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var modifiedHuberGradient = require( '@stdlib/ml/base/loss/float32/modified-huber-gradient' );
```

#### modifiedHuberGradient( x, y, p )

Computes the [modified Huber loss gradient][modified-huber-loss-gradient] with respect to a model parameter for a single-precision floating-point number.

```javascript
var v = modifiedHuberGradient( 3.4, 1.0, 0.782 );
// returns ~-1.482

v = modifiedHuberGradient( 2.3, 1.0, -0.999 );
// returns ~-9.195
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **x**: input value.
-   **y**: true target value.
-   **p**: predicted value.

If any argument is `NaN`, the function returns `NaN`.

```javascript
var v = modifiedHuberGradient( NaN, 1.0, 0.782 );
// returns NaN

v = modifiedHuberGradient( 1.0, NaN, 0.782 );
// returns NaN

v = modifiedHuberGradient( 1.0, 1.0, NaN );
// returns NaN

v = modifiedHuberGradient( NaN, NaN, NaN );
// returns NaN
```

If `y` is not +1 or -1, the function returns `NaN`.

```javascript
var v = modifiedHuberGradient( 3.0, -0.9, 1.0 );
// returns NaN

v = modifiedHuberGradient( 4.0, 0.453, 0.76 );
// returns NaN
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var uniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/uniform' );
var sample = require( '@stdlib/random/sample' );
var logEachMap = require( '@stdlib/console/log-each-map' );
var modifiedHuberGradient = require( '@stdlib/ml/base/loss/float32/modified-huber-gradient' );

var x = uniform( 100, -10.0, 10.0, {
    'dtype': 'float32'
});
var y = sample( [ -1.0, 1.0 ], {
    'size': 100
});
var p = uniform( 100, -5.0, 5.0, {
    'dtype': 'float32'
});

logEachMap( 'modifiedHuberGradient(%0.4f, %0.4f, %0.4f) = %0.4f', x, y, p, modifiedHuberGradient );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/ml/base/loss/float32/modified_huber_gradient.h"
```

#### stdlib_base_float32_modified_huber_gradient( x, y, p )

Computes the [modified Huber loss gradient][modified-huber-loss-gradient] with respect to a model parameter for a single-precision floating-point number.

```c
float out = stdlib_base_float32_modified_huber_gradient( 3.4f, 1.0f, 0.782f );
// returns ~-1.482f
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **x**: `[in] float` input value.
-   **y**: `[in] float` true target value.
-   **p**: `[in] float` predicted value.

```c
float stdlib_base_float32_modified_huber_gradient( const float x, const float y, const float p );
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- C API usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/ml/base/loss/float32/modified_huber_gradient.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main( void ) {
    const float x[] = { 1.0f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 5.0f, 6.0f, 7.0f, 8.0f, 9.0f, 10.0f };
    const float y[] = { -1.0f, -1.0f, -1.0f, -1.0f, -1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f };
    const float p[] = { -5.0f, -3.89f, -2.78f, -1.67f, -0.56f, 0.56f, 1.67f, 2.78f, 3.89f, 5.0f };

    float v;
    int i;
    for ( i = 0; i < 10; i++ ) {
        v = stdlib_base_float32_modified_huber_gradient( x[ i ], y[ i ], p[ i ] );
        printf( "modifiedHuberGradient(%f, %f, %f) = %f\n", x[ i ], y[ i ], p[ i ], v );
    }
}
```

</section>
